1.explanation:
All of the logic that drives the special title‐slide markup and layout for Quarto‐generated revealjs decks lives under `src/format/reveal/`.  

• metadata.ts declares the `hash-type` option (and its default) that you toggle between “number” and “title”.  If that metadata entry accidentally prevents Quarto from recognizing a title‐slide generation pass, you’ll get the generic reveal.js default (centered).  

• format-reveal.ts reads the user metadata (including `hash-type`) and decides whether to invoke the title‐slide generator at all — it wires up Reveal.initialize() plus the custom slide sections.  

• format-reveal-title.ts actually emits the HTML/CSS for Quarto’s fancy title slide (with left‐aligned text, right‐positioned author info, etc.).  In the buggy code path, that file never gets applied when `hash-type` is set to “number”.  

Fixing this behavior will require adjusting metadata.ts (so that “number” does not disable the title‐slide path), format-reveal.ts (so it always calls format-reveal-title regardless of hash type), or the guard inside format-reveal-title.ts that skips applying the custom template when hash-type isn’t “title.”
1.bug_scenario: When you set your Quarto revealjs slide option to `hash-type: number`, the very first (title) slide no longer uses Quarto’s custom title‐slide HTML/CSS and instead falls back to reveal.js’s generic centered‐content template.  You lose the author‐on‐the‐right layout, the left‐aligned title/subtitle, etc.  By contrast, `hash-type: title` correctly triggers Quarto’s custom title‐slide generator and the layout is right every time.

2.explanation:
All of the affected behavior is controlled in the Quarto TypeScript modules that define the revealjs output and in particular the title-slide generation and hash-type wiring. 

• src/format/reveal/metadata.ts declares the new hash-type metadata (number vs. title) but currently only wires it through as a Pandoc option – it needs to correctly emit the matching Reveal.js config so that the hash setting is honored.

• src/format/reveal/constants.ts contains the default Reveal.js configuration and CSS classes used by Quarto for centering the title slide. Changing hash-type should not override or drop these defaults, but currently the numeric IDs prevent the title-slide class or data-state hook from being applied as expected.

• src/format/reveal/format-reveal.ts is the central formatter that reads the metadata and passes options into Reveal.initialize(). It must translate the new hash-type into the proper Reveal.js “hash” value (e.g. {hash: true, hashMode: 'number'} or equivalent) so that the URL hashing logic does not break the centering CSS rules.

• src/format/reveal/format-reveal-title.ts actually generates the <section> wrapper for the title slide and applies the CSS class that triggers centering. When hash-type is set to number it currently falls back to a plain <section id="1"> without the .title-slide wrapper, so the slide content never gets the CSS that vertically/horizontally centers it. Adjusting this module will restore the wrapper regardless of which hash-type is chosen.
2.bug_scenario: When the user sets format.revealjs.hash-type to “number” the first (title) slide is no longer centered. All of the title, subtitle, author and date content collapse up into the top-left corner of the viewport (see Broken_Version), whereas with hash-type “title” the slide remains perfectly centered (see Working_Version). In other words, switching the revealjs hash-type causes the title-slide wrapper or its CSS hook to lose the centering CSS and fall back to normal flow positioning.
